rows.title: Tidal islet in Eddrachillis Bay
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says Calbha Mòr is a tidal islet in Eddrachillis Bay.
rows.summary: Calbha Mòr is a tidal islet in Eddrachillis Bay, Sutherland, Scotland.

rows.title: Land bridge from Herm
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says Caquorobert can be reached from Herm on foot at low tide by a land bridge, and that a gully on the crossing is submerged under the tide.
rows.summary: The island can be accessed from Herm on foot at low tide from the round-island Cliff Path. There is a track down to what, at low tide, is a land bridge over to the island. A gully on the western side is fully submerged under the tide.

rows.title: Tidal island near Copinsay
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says Corn Holm is a small tidal island in Orkney, near Copinsay.
rows.summary: Corn Holm is a small tidal island in Orkney, near Copinsay to the west, off the north-eastern coast of Scotland.

rows.title: Tidal island in the Dornoch Firth
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says Innis Mhòr is a tidal island in the Dornoch Firth, with the tidal Whiteness Sands between it and the Easter Ross coast.
rows.summary: Innis Mhòr is a tidal island in the Dornoch Firth of Easter Ross off the east coast of Scotland. The extensive tidal Whiteness Sands lie between Innis Mhòr and the Easter Ross coast.

rows.title: Tidal island in Portelet Bay
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says Portelet Tower stands on the tidal island L'Île au Guerdain, also called Janvrin's Tomb, and that the site is accessible at low tide.
rows.summary: Portelet Tower, Jersey, is a round tower that the British built in 1808 on the tidal island L'Île au Guerdain in Portelet Bay. The site is often referred to as Janvrin's Tomb. The site is accessible at low tide.

rows.title: Tidal island in Loch Dunvegan
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says Lampay is an uninhabited tidal island in Loch Dunvegan, off Skye.
rows.summary: Lampay is an uninhabited tidal island in Loch Dunvegan, off the northwest coast of the Isle of Skye in Scotland.

rows.title: Joined at low tide, apart when the tide is higher
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says Lunga is made of several parts that are connected at low tides and separate at higher states of the tide.
rows.summary: Lunga is a complex island made of several separate parts that are connected at low tides but which "disintegrate" at higher states of the tidal cycle.

rows.title: Tidal island at Eddrachillis Bay
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says Oldany Island is a large tidal island at the southwestern entrance to Eddrachillis Bay.
rows.summary: Oldany Island is a large tidal island at the southwestern entrance to Eddrachillis Bay/Kylesku.

rows.title: Tidal island off North Uist
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says Oronsay (Orasaigh) is a tidal island off North Uist, lying north of Vallaquie Strand.
rows.summary: Oronsay (Gaelic Orasaigh) is a tidal island off North Uist in the Outer Hebrides. Lying to the north of Vallaquie Strand, the island has been uninhabited since the Highland Clearances.

rows.title: Joined to Yell
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says Orfasay is a tidal island in Yell Sound, connected to Yell at low tide.
rows.summary: Orfasay is a tidal island in Yell Sound, connected to Yell at low tide.

rows.title: Separated from Caldey at high tide
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says St Margaret's Island is a tidal island, separated from Caldey at high tide, with foot access from Caldey at low tide.
rows.summary: St Margaret's Island is a small tidal island to the northwest of Caldey Island in Carmarthen Bay, Pembrokeshire, Wales. At high tide the island is separated from Caldey Island by Little Sound. There is no public access to the island; access on foot from Caldey at low tide is dangerous.

rows.title: Tidal island off Papa
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says West Head of Papa is a small tidal island off Papa in Shetland.
rows.summary: West Head of Papa is a small tidal island off Papa in Shetland, and is one of the Scalloway Islands.

rows.title: No tidal sentence
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia describes Achillbeg as a small island off Achill. It does not say the island is joined at low tide and cut off at high tide.
rows.reject_reason: The island's own article has no joined-and-cut-off sentence.
rows.summary: Achillbeg is a small island in County Mayo, just off the southern tip of Achill Island.

rows.title: Permanent causeway
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says the British built the existing causeway, and that land access is still by that causeway.
rows.reject_reason: Permanent causeway. The page does not say the crossing is cut at high tide.
rows.summary: The British built the existing causeway to County Galway. Land access to Aughinish is still only through County Galway.

rows.title: No crossing sentence
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia gives an area that possibly includes ground exposed at low tide. It does not say this island is joined to another shore and cut off at high tide.
rows.reject_reason: A low-tide area note is not a crossing that floods.
rows.summary: An estimate of the area possibly includes areas exposed at low tide.

rows.title: Only extreme low tides
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says extreme low tides would allow land access to Calve, via the small tidal island of Cnap a' Chailbhe.
rows.reject_reason: Only extreme low tides, and the walk named is via neighbouring Cnap a' Chailbhe.
rows.summary: Calve is classed as a separate island from Mull, although at its south-western point there are extreme low tides that would allow land access to it, via the small tidal island of Cnap a' Chailbhe.

rows.title: No tidal sentence
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia describes Carna in Loch Sunart. It does not say the island is joined at low tide and cut off at high tide.
rows.reject_reason: The island's own article has no joined-and-cut-off sentence.
rows.summary: Carna or Càrna is an island in Loch Sunart, an arm of the sea, close to the Ardnamurchan peninsula.

rows.title: Connected at low tide only
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says Ceann Iar is connected at low tide to Ceann Ear via Sibhinis. It does not say the link is cut off at high tide.
rows.reject_reason: The own article does not say both joined at low tide and cut off at high tide.
rows.summary: It is connected at low tide to Ceann Ear via Sibhinis.

rows.title: Permanent road causeway
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says Eilean na Cille is connected to Grimsay by a causeway which carries the B891.
rows.reject_reason: Permanent road causeway.
rows.summary: Eilean na Cille, south east of Benbecula, is connected to Grimsay (South) by a causeway which carries the B891.

rows.title: Bridge
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia calls Eriska a tidal island, then refers to the bridge as a fixed feature and does not say the crossing is cut at high tide.
rows.reject_reason: The page describes a bridge and does not say it is covered at high tide.
rows.summary: Eriska is a relatively flat tidal island at the entrance to Loch Creran. To the east of the bridge, there is a partly submerged crannog.

rows.title: Walkable at most times
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says Fenit Island is accessible by foot along the sandbar at most times, and by car at low tide.
rows.reject_reason: Foot access at most times means the island is not cut off at high tide.
rows.summary: The island is accessible by foot along the sandbar at most times, and by car at low tide, by driving on the beach.

rows.title: Causeway not said to flood
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia calls Flodaigh a tidal island connected to Benbecula by a causeway, and does not say the causeway is covered at high tide.
rows.reject_reason: Causeway not described as covered at high tide.
rows.summary: Flodaigh is a tidal island lying to the north of Benbecula and south of Grimsay. It is connected to Benbecula by a causeway.

rows.title: Causeway covered, no atlas island
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says Fort Clonque is joined to Alderney by a causeway that can be submerged at high tide. No matching island is in the atlas.
rows.reject_reason: No island_id in the atlas.
rows.summary: Fort Clonque is built on a rocky outcrop of land joined to the island by a causeway that can be submerged at high tide.

rows.title: Permanent bridge
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says Gometra is linked to Ulva by a bridge, and at low tide also by a beach.
rows.reject_reason: Permanent bridge.
rows.summary: It lies immediately west of Ulva, to which it is linked by a bridge, and at low tide also by a beach.

rows.title: Permanent road causeway
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia calls Grimsay a tidal island, then says the North Ford causeway is a single-track road, opened in 1960, linking North Uist and Benbecula.
rows.reject_reason: The tidal ford was replaced by a permanent road causeway.
rows.summary: Grimsay is the largest of the low-lying stepping-stones which convey the Oitir Mhòr (North Ford) causeway, a five-mile arc of single track road linking North Uist and Benbecula.

rows.title: Permanent B891 causeway
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says this Grimsay is connected to Benbecula by a causeway which carries the B891.
rows.reject_reason: Permanent road causeway.
rows.summary: Grimsay, south east of Benbecula is a tidal island of the Outer Hebrides. It is connected to Benbecula by a causeway which carries the B891.

rows.title: Distance at low tide, not a crossing
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says that at low tide Harlosh Island is about 100 metres from Harlosh Point. It does not say the gap can be walked or that it closes at high tide.
rows.reject_reason: A shorter gap at low tide is not a crossing that floods.
rows.summary: At low tide it is only about 100 metres from Harlosh Point on mainland Skye.

rows.title: No tidal sentence
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia describes Hildasay as an uninhabited island off the Shetland Mainland. It does not say Hildasay itself is joined at low tide and cut off at high tide.
rows.reject_reason: The island's own article has no joined-and-cut-off sentence.
rows.summary: Hildasay is an uninhabited island off the west coast of the Shetland Mainland.

rows.title: Causeway not said to flood
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia calls Holm of Grimbister a tidal islet connected to Mainland Orkney by a causeway, and does not say the causeway is covered at high tide.
rows.reject_reason: Causeway not described as covered at high tide.
rows.summary: Holm of Grimbister is an inhabited tidal islet in the Orkney archipelago of Scotland. Located in the Bay of Firth near Finstown it is connected to Mainland Orkney by a causeway.

rows.title: No tidal sentence
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia describes Kirkibost as a low-lying island west of North Uist. It does not say the island is joined at low tide and cut off at high tide.
rows.reject_reason: The island's own article has no joined-and-cut-off sentence.
rows.summary: Kirkibost is a low-lying island west of North Uist in the Outer Hebrides of Scotland.

rows.title: No tidal sentence
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia describes Long Island, County Cork. It does not say the island is joined at low tide and cut off at high tide.
rows.reject_reason: The island's own article has no joined-and-cut-off sentence.
rows.summary: Long Island is an island that lies south of Schull, County Cork, Ireland.

rows.title: Separated by a sound
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says Middleholm is separated from the mainland by Jack Sound and from Skomer by Little Sound. It does not say either sound can be walked at low tide.
rows.reject_reason: The sounds are not described as a crossing that dries.
rows.summary: It is separated from the mainland by Jack Sound and from Skomer by Little Sound.

rows.title: Called a peninsula
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia calls Mochras, also known as Shell Island, a peninsula. The list of islands of Wales sets it aside from the tidal islands.
rows.reject_reason: The island's own article calls it a peninsula.
rows.summary: Mochras, also known in English as Shell Island, is a peninsula lying west of Llanbedr in Gwynedd, Wales.

rows.title: Causeway not said to flood
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia calls St Patrick's Isle a tidal island, then says it is connected to Peel by a causeway, and does not say the causeway is covered at high tide.
rows.reject_reason: Causeway not described as covered at high tide.
rows.summary: It is connected to the town of Peel on the Isle of Man by a causeway over Fenella Beach.

rows.title: Permanent road bridge
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says Sanday is linked to Canna by sandbanks at low tide and by a road bridge that allows access at all tide levels.
rows.reject_reason: Permanent bridge. The road bridge is open at all tide levels.
rows.summary: It is a tidal island linked to its larger neighbour, Canna, via sandbanks at low tide, and also connected to the larger island by a bridge. This new bridge allows vehicular access at all tide levels between the two islands.

rows.title: No tidal sentence
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia describes Seaforth Island in Loch Seaforth. It does not say the island is joined at low tide and cut off at high tide.
rows.reject_reason: The island's own article has no joined-and-cut-off sentence.
rows.summary: Seaforth Island is an uninhabited island in the Outer Hebrides of Scotland.

rows.title: The low-tide walk is not this island
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says the adjacent Soay Beag is accessible on foot at low tide. It does not say Soay Mòr itself is joined and cut off.
rows.reject_reason: The low-tide sentence names neighbouring Soay Beag.
rows.summary: The adjacent Soay Beag is accessible on foot at low tide.

rows.title: Tombolo not reliably cut off
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says the tombolo is above sea level and walkable in summer, and usually covered at high tide in winter. It does not say the island is cut off at high tide as a rule.
rows.reject_reason: The own article does not say the crossing is cut off at high tide in ordinary conditions.
rows.summary: During the summer the tombolo is above sea level and accessible to walkers. During winter, stronger wave action removes sand from the beach so that it is usually covered at high tide.

rows.title: No atlas island
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says St Twrog's Island is a small tidal island and that access is frequently cut off by the tide. No matching island is in the atlas.
rows.reject_reason: No island_id in the atlas.
rows.summary: St Twrog's Island is a small tidal island in the Severn estuary. Access to the island is frequently cut off by the tidal waters of the estuary.

rows.title: No tidal sentence
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia describes Thorne Island as a rocky islet with a coastal fort. It does not say the island is joined at low tide and cut off at high tide.
rows.reject_reason: The island's own article has no joined-and-cut-off sentence.
rows.summary: Thorne Island is a rocky islet and part of the community of Angle, Pembrokeshire, Wales, dominated by a coastal artillery fort.

rows.title: Fordable at low water only
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia calls Torsa a tidal island and says a narrow strait is fordable at low water. It does not say the strait is cut off at high tide.
rows.reject_reason: The own article does not say both joined at low tide and cut off at high tide.
rows.summary: A rough track leads down to a narrow strait, fordable at low water, and onto the south west corner of the island.

rows.title: No tidal-island sentence
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia describes Uyea, south of Unst. It does not say this Uyea is joined at low tide and cut off at high tide.
rows.reject_reason: The island's own article has no joined-and-cut-off sentence. This is not the Northmavine Uyea already filed.
rows.summary: Uyea is an uninhabited island, lying south of Unst in Shetland, Scotland.

rows.title: No crossing to the mainland
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says Ynys Dulas lies about a mile and a half offshore, and that sand exposed at low tide separates its own rocks. It does not say a crossing from the mainland is cut at high tide.
rows.reject_reason: Offshore rock. The low-tide sand is between parts of the island, not a crossing from the shore.
rows.summary: The island is situated about a mile and a half offshore. At low tide sand is exposed, most noticeably on the southern part of the island where it separates the main rock formation from two smaller ones.

rows.title: Bridge and causeway
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says Ynys Gaint is connected to Menai Bridge by a causeway which still exists and by a concrete bridge.
rows.reject_reason: Permanent causeway and bridge.
rows.summary: Ynys Gaint is a small island in the Menai Strait connected to the town of Menai Bridge on Anglesey by a causeway (which still exists today) and also a concrete bridge.

rows.title: No atlas island for Llanddwyn itself
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says Ynys Llanddwyn is a tidal island and remains attached to the mainland except at high tide. The atlas has no island under this name. Nearby skerries are not Llanddwyn.
rows.reject_reason: The sentence is about Llanddwyn. There is no matching island_id. Not filed on a neighbouring skerry.
rows.summary: Ynys Llanddwyn is a small tidal island off the west coast of Anglesey. It remains attached to the mainland except at high tide.
